page: Amazon Web Services m8id.48xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 192 vCPUs and 96 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors running at 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes 11,400 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 75 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core, Passmark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers top-tier read and write bandwidth, reaching 15,316.45 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 587.33 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-core performance represents a relative tradeoff, with stress-ng single-core results falling into the average middle 50% tier. The processor's Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) contribute to top-tier performance in extended instructions, encryption, and LLM inference prompt processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m8id.48xlarge offers high resource density by combining massive compute capacity, high-speed DDR5 memory, and substantial local NVMe SSD storage within a single general-purpose footprint. This hardware profile is highly suited for large-scale database operations, multi-threaded software compilation, high-throughput static web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference workloads.
